correctness.rationale: The two positive phase equations give (a_i−1)(b_i−1)=1 and then a_i=a_{i+1}; conversely r>1 and s=r/(r−1) give all such states, including the fixed state at r=2. Fourier reduction of the product of the two step derivatives gives trace q+q²d and determinant q²d. The Schur–Cohn margin is 2d(1−cos θ)[1−2d−(1+2cos θ)d²], with the bracket at least 5/16. The only neutral root is the simple tangent root at q=1. In coordinates along and across the fixed curve, choose an adapted norm for the transverse derivative at the selected point and shrink the neighborhood to get uniform contraction there. The summed tangential increments are bounded by a geometric series, so sufficiently close points stay in the neighborhood and converge exponentially to a member; no global basin is implied. Implicit differentiation gives λ′(1)=1/(1−d) and λ″(1)=2d(1−2d)/(1−d)³. The even analytic modulus has quadratic decrement d(1−3d)/(2(1−d)³)>0 and fourth-order remainder. Compactness away from q=1 and strict local monotonicity select q=exp(±2πi/k) for large k. At fixed k the root through q is q+(q²−q)d+O(d²) and the other root tends to zero; the stated small-d maximum follows.
